concepts.name: Six tones and tone marks
concepts.summary: Recognise the six tones (ngang, huyền, sắc, hỏi, ngã, nặng), match each to its mark, and understand that tone changes word meaning, as in ma, má, mà, mả, mã, mạ.

concepts.name: Quốc ngữ vowels and đ
concepts.summary: Remember the special letters ă, â, ê, ô, ơ, ư and đ and the sounds they represent, distinct from a, e, o, u, d.

concepts.name: Syllable structure and spelling
concepts.summary: Understand that each written syllable is separated by spaces, is built from an initial, vowel, final and tone, and is pronounced largely as written.

concepts.name: Core personal pronouns
concepts.summary: Understand that tôi and bạn are neutral, while anh, chị and em signal relative age and gender.

concepts.name: Basic greetings and politeness
concepts.summary: Recall core phrases such as xin chào, cảm ơn, xin lỗi, vâng and không, and use them in simple exchanges.

concepts.name: Subject-verb-object word order
concepts.summary: Understand that simple sentences follow subject-verb-object order and that verbs never change form.

concepts.name: Copula là and negation không
concepts.summary: Understand that là links nouns (Tôi là sinh viên) and that không before a verb or adjective negates it.

misconceptions.text: Tone marks are optional accents that can be dropped without changing the meaning.
Vietnamese letters like đ, ơ and ư are just stylistic variants of d, o and u.
Each Vietnamese word is one syllable and there are no multi-syllable words.

concepts.name: Kinship pronouns by age and rank
concepts.summary: Choose anh, chị, em, cô, chú, bác, ông, bà for self and addressee according to relative age, gender and relationship.

concepts.name: Classifiers cái and con
concepts.summary: Use cái for inanimate objects, con for animals and some others, and other classifiers such as người, quyển, chiếc, with numbers and demonstratives.

concepts.name: Tense and aspect particles
concepts.summary: Use đã, đang, sẽ and vừa to express past, ongoing and future events, dropping them when time words make the time clear.

concepts.name: Question words and particles
concepts.summary: Form yes-no questions with có...không and wh-questions with gì, ai, đâu, khi nào, bao nhiêu in the right position.

concepts.name: Adjectives as predicates
concepts.summary: Understand that adjectives act as verbs without là, as in Cô ấy rất đẹp, and use degree words like rất and quá.

concepts.name: Numbers and noun phrase order
concepts.summary: Build noun phrases in the order number, classifier, noun, adjective, demonstrative, such as hai con mèo đen này.

concepts.name: Northern and southern accent differences
concepts.summary: Recognise main differences such as the Hanoi merging of d/gi/r and the southern merging of hỏi and ngã tones and distinct vocabulary.

misconceptions.text: Verbs must take đã, đang or sẽ to show tense, as with English tense endings.
Classifiers are optional decoration and can be left out of counting phrases.
Adjectives need là in front of them, as in Cô ấy là đẹp.

concepts.name: Compound and reduplicative words
concepts.summary: Analyse how compound words and reduplicatives (đẹp đẽ, xinh xắn) are formed and use them to vary tone and register.

concepts.name: Sentence-final and discourse particles
concepts.summary: Distinguish the pragmatic effect of particles like nhé, nhỉ, à, ạ, đâu and mà, and choose them to soften, confirm or emphasise.

concepts.name: Complex sentences and connectors
concepts.summary: Link clauses with vì...nên, nếu...thì, mặc dù...nhưng, để and khi to express cause, condition, concession and purpose.

concepts.name: Passive and adversity constructions
concepts.summary: Contrast bị for adverse and được for beneficial events and recognise when each marks a passive meaning.

concepts.name: Directional and resultative verbs
concepts.summary: Combine main verbs with ra, vào, lên, xuống, về, đi, lại, and with resultative complements like xong and được.

concepts.name: Topic-comment structure and ellipsis
concepts.summary: Analyse how topics are fronted and subjects or pronouns omitted when context makes them clear.

concepts.name: Comparison and degree structures
concepts.summary: Express comparison with hơn, bằng, như, nhất and không bằng, and with degree words such as hơi, khá and quá.

misconceptions.text: Bị and được are interchangeable ways of saying passive with no difference in nuance.
Sentence-final particles carry no meaning and can be freely omitted or swapped.
Every sentence must have an explicit subject, so dropping pronouns is incorrect.

concepts.name: Register and honorific selection
concepts.summary: Judge and adjust pronouns, particles and vocabulary for formality, relationship and situation, and repair mismatches.

concepts.name: Sino-Vietnamese vocabulary
concepts.summary: Analyse how Sino-Vietnamese roots form formal, academic and abstract terms, contrasted with native Vietnamese equivalents.

concepts.name: Dialect vocabulary and tone variation
concepts.summary: Compare northern, central and southern lexicon, tone inventories and final consonant pronunciation and decode them in listening.

concepts.name: Idioms and proverbs
concepts.summary: Interpret common thành ngữ and tục ngữ with their cultural imagery and use them appropriately.

concepts.name: Text cohesion and argumentation
concepts.summary: Evaluate how connectors, pronoun reference and parallelism build coherent essays, reports and arguments.

concepts.name: Pragmatics of indirectness and face
concepts.summary: Evaluate how indirect refusals, hedging and humility reflect social hierarchy and face in conversation.

concepts.name: Loanwords and borrowed terms
concepts.summary: Analyse the sources and adaptation of French and English loanwords and when native or borrowed terms are preferred.

misconceptions.text: Sino-Vietnamese words are Chinese and not really part of Vietnamese.
Using a single polite pronoun pair is enough for formality in every context.
A direct translation of idioms from English keeps the same meaning and tone.

concepts.name: Stylistic choice in literary Vietnamese
concepts.summary: Craft prose or verse that deliberately uses Hán Việt, reduplication, rhythm and parallelism for effect.

concepts.name: Pronoun strategy in narrative voice
concepts.summary: Design address-term systems that convey character relationships, shifts in intimacy and power in narrative or subtitling.

concepts.name: Translation and equivalence judgment
concepts.summary: Evaluate translations for handling of pronouns, classifiers, tense, register and cultural references and justify alternatives.

concepts.name: Poetic forms and tonal prosody
concepts.summary: Compose in forms such as lục bát using the bằng-trắc tone patterns and rhyme rules.

concepts.name: Language change and standardisation
concepts.summary: Evaluate the history of quốc ngữ, debates on standard pronunciation and spelling, and emerging usage such as online slang.

concepts.name: Adapting speech across dialect audiences
concepts.summary: Create or adapt spoken and written material for northern, central and southern audiences, choosing lexicon and pronunciation intentionally.

misconceptions.text: A good translation maps each English pronoun to a single fixed Vietnamese pronoun.
Hanoi speech is the only correct Vietnamese and other accents are errors.
Lục bát only requires counting syllables, not tone patterns.
